issues.title: quick & incomplete review of the editor’s copy
issues.author: thomas-fossati
issues.body:
### General comments

We should either s/transport/secure transport/g or establish the equivalence of the terms (within the scope of this document) very early on.

We could add somewhere Gene Spafford's usual quote: "Cryptography [without system integrity] is like investing in an armored car to carry money between a customer living in a cardboard box and a person doing business on a park bench." :-)  An rfcxml "aside" should do the trick.

We need "moar pics!"

### §2

Verification Anchor def: seems to bias towards intra- ("typically")

Layered Attestation def: the fact that the TCB is layered should be an internal detail.

### §3.1

It says: "the Attesting Environment MUST NOT treat an attestation binder input received from an untrusted host as authoritative without first verifying it has not been substituted."
This seems predicated on the Attesting Environment's ability to continuously monitor the extended TCB state and assess its trustworthiness every time the binder is sent across the TE/AE boundary.
I guess we could remove some of the current vagueness by making the requirements for the AE explicit.

### §3.3

It says: "In the transport context, two deployment variants arise that correspond to the topological timing models defined in Section 5"
The coupling between the arrangement of RATS roles and the timing models seems unwarranted.
It also creates some dissonance with §5.3, "Combining Timing Models".

### §4.4

This one's a tough cookie :-)

It is unclear what "eviction" and "eviction signalling" refer to.  They don't seem to appear anywhere else.

It says" "[...] transport-layer routing obligations" which seems to downplay what a real L7 device can do somewhat.

### §5

I'd add a reference to the paper by Arto et al. that introduced the pre-/intra-/post- nomenclature: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1007/978-3-030-91625-1_10

### §5.2

It says: "Post-handshake is an application-layer mechanism."
It is unclear what "mechanism" is supposed to mean in this context.

### 6.1

This breaks the e2e invariant provided by the secure transport layer, requiring a new way to establish the broken e2e invariant at a higher layer.
This increases the complexity of implementation and deployment, and therefore fragility.
Do we really want to go there?

The term "out-of-band" doesn't sound entirely appropriate. I believe the proxy is still assumed to be on-path, no?

comments.author: telephonicrobotics
comments.body:
Thanks for the review! I'm going to jump on the most contentious part and address the others in a separate reply. 

> ### §4.4
> This one's a tough cookie :-)
> 
> It is unclear what "eviction" and "eviction signalling" refer to. They don't seem to appear anywhere else.
> 
> It says" "[...] transport-layer routing obligations" which seems to downplay what a real L7 device can do somewhat.
> 
> <snip>
> ### 6.1
> This breaks the e2e invariant provided by the secure transport layer, requiring a new way to establish the broken e2e invariant at a higher layer. This increases the complexity of implementation and deployment, and therefore fragility.

>  Do we really want to go there?

As it turns out, yes, kinda (I do). I've roped Hannes in on the idea with some enthusiasm (and Ionut has humoured me, and I also invited Tiru in on it not super long ago-- who may or may not agree). It makes use of [EKU ](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-tls-extended-key-update/). However; I will repeat what I shared with Markus at https://github.com/tls-attestation/use-cases-and-properties/pull/48#issuecomment-4687308877 : 

"I have a concept for how to allow an attestation aware proxy to cooperate without requiring nested encryption, but if that was not to pan out for any number of reasons, then the property would basically just affirm that the protocol should abort the connection if intercepted by a malicious intermediary."

However-- these parts of the review make it clear that these sections needs additional abstractions and smoothing over from stuff that was borrowed over from my other draft I mentioned, so I'll prioritize that to minimize distractions on this document.

pulls.title: Add Dynamic Verification Code Integrity considerations per Ekr
pulls.author: telephonicrobotics
pulls.body:
Incorporate concerns raised by Ekr [on-list](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/seat/-wOnrqnQZPY4s19y7_Kj1zifwn0/).

In part: "[...] I don't see how anything implemented in browser-based JS can provide any kind of assurance unless there is *also* some form of assurance for the JS itself [[0]](https://realworldcrypto.iacr.org/2026/program.php). Otherwise, the attester (who, remember, is the attacker) can just serve JS that pretends to verify the proofs."
